messages:
sara: Quick note 12h trend: inbound SLA miss rate up during the webinar traffic spike. Thinking: emergency throttle + adaptive enrichment priority for webinar leads. Also a fallback handoff policy for high-intent webinar signups. Thoughts?

mike: For webinar leads we should bypass heavy enrichment for first-touch and route directly to SDRs if intent_flag == true. Can do a special workflow.

julio: Agree but need to limit to leads with email domain not in blacklist and lead_score >= 0.35. Also set a TTL for bypassed enrichment to allow later enrichment to patch missing fields.

gino: Sales ops: prefer using a separate rotation pool for webinar traffic so reps opt-in. Also want to avoid cannibalizing normal pipeline.

hubspot-bot: Created workflow: webinar-bypass-canary (id:99888)

sara: Plan: 10m owner hold, then if owner not responded, route to webinar_rotation pool. Only apply to leads with intent_flag==true AND not from list suppression. Dry-run first hour.

mike: Add SFDC dedupe and no-convert guard. Also include a custom property `webinar_source = true` so downstream analytics can filter.

julio: I'll prepare the list of blocked domains and the scoring update. Also TTL = 6h for bypass tag.

sara: Owners: mike = workflow + SFDC guard, julio = scoring and domain blocklist, gino = rotation opt-in + capacity rules, sara = monitoring and rollback criteria. Canary go-live 48h after dry-run.

gino: I'll set rotation.max_claims_per_hour = 2 for webinar pool and skip reps with last_claim_at < 30m.

mike: Rollback triggers: webinar_claim_churn > 2% or drop in webinar MQL conversions > 2ppt.

sara: Add to runbook: disable workflow, remove `webinar_source` tags, notify #marketing and #sales.

julio: logging: emit event for `webinar_bypass_event` with original_enrichment_status and claim_method.

sara: Good. Scheduling ticket now.
